paper.title: Microplastics in municipal drinking water: a national survey

paper_text:
Microplastics in municipal drinking water: a national survey
Becker, F., Ito, M.  J. Fake Environmental Health, 2020

Abstract
Microplastic particles were found in 83% of 400 tap-water samples from 40 cities.

alerts.description: An expression of concern was published for this paper.
A notice of type removal was published for this paper.

documents.text:
Expression of concern: Microplastics in municipal drinking water: a national survey

The editors have been alerted to concerns about possible contamination of the water samples and are looking into the matter.

Removal of expression of concern: Microplastics in municipal drinking water: a national survey

The editors have completed their review, with an independent laboratory re-testing retained samples. The contamination concerns were not substantiated and the findings of the article are confirmed. The expression of concern published earlier is removed.

draft_text:
Exposure to microplastics through tap water

1. Introduction
Microplastics are widespread in tap water: 83% of samples contained particles (Becker and Ito [2]), which is the starting point of our exposure model.

References
[2] Becker, F., Ito, M. (2020). Microplastics in municipal drinking water: a national survey. J. Fake Environmental Health.

expected.why: Rubric: a concern lifted by a later notice in the same report is none, and report severity is lower than the highest alert when a later notice resolves an earlier one. Both alerts carry a non-trivial alert_severity from the rules, so a model that just takes the highest alert says medium. Severity none stops the pipeline before the draft is read.
